TD.notes: TD reports Prairies combined (no Alberta split). HELOC = insured + uninsured HELOC (4,619 + 172,583). TD's HELOCs include the non-amortizing part of combined plans, so its HELOC share is much higher than peers; compare on total RESL.

CIBC.source: CIBC Q3 2026 Report to Shareholders (SEC 6-K ex. 99.1), B-20 residential mortgage and HELOC table
CIBC.notes: Published in C$ billions to one decimal. 'Central prairie provinces' = Manitoba and Saskatchewan.

NBC.source: National Bank Q3 2026 Supplementary Financial Information (xlsx), sheet 26 'Residential Mortgages Portfolios Information' — Retail Canada by region
NBC.notes: Retail residential only (excludes $22.4B non-retail 5+ unit and commercial 1–4 unit residential mortgages, and U.S./Cambodia retail). Atlantic = New Brunswick + 'Other Canadian provinces' (PE, NS, NL, NT, YT); BC excludes territories. Prior quarters back to Q2 2025 are in the same file.

DESJ.source: Desjardins Q3 2026 interim report (quarter ended September 30, 2026), residential mortgage portfolio table, p. 33: caisse network in Quebec and Caisse Desjardins Ontario Credit Union Inc. Guaranteed or insured $33,095M, uninsured $115,570M, HELOC $6,505M, total $155,170M. Quebec $148,163M, Ontario $6,936M, other provinces $71M.
DESJ.notes: Caisse network (Quebec caisses plus Caisse Desjardins Ontario Credit Union Inc.), as reported by Desjardins. The regional split is reported, not estimated. Other provinces ($0.07B) are not shown in the regional split but are in the total. Excludes about $0.2B of up-to-four-unit mortgages held outside the caisse network. The Q2 2026 version of this figure used an estimated split that overstated Ontario. Regulated by Quebec's AMF, not OSFI.

l2.harmonization: Prairies = Alberta + Saskatchewan + Manitoba (BMO's "All other Canada" also includes the territories). B.C. includes the territories except at National Bank, whose territories sit in Atlantic. National Bank figures are retail only.

meta.b20Source: each bank's Q3 2026 quarterly report or supplementary package (quarter ended July 31, 2026)
meta.leagueIntl: about $55B at Scotiabank, $47B at TD, $41B at RBC and $33B at BMO
meta.leagueNote: TD's HELOC figure includes the non-amortizing part of its combined plans, so its HELOC share is much higher than other banks'. Compare banks on the total.
meta.profNote: Most banks have an October fiscal year end; Equitable Bank's is December, and its year-to-date figures include about $0.4B of provisions, most of it booked in its third quarter.
meta.cet1Note: CET1 capital as a share of risk-weighted assets, from each bank's quarterly Basel III capital return. The dashed line is today's 11.0% floor for Canada's six big banks: the 8% CET1 minimum for systemically important banks plus OSFI's 3.0% Domestic Stability Buffer, which OSFI lowered from 3.5% in June 2026. Earlier years had different buffer levels, so the line shows the current requirement, not the historical one.
meta.dataNotes: All-banks totals for Q3 2026 (quarter and year to date) were blanked in this file because they were below the sum of the seven banks listed, which means they were incomplete. Nothing on the dashboard uses them. Re-add once OSFI's P3 returns for all banks are published.
